## Higher-detail sculptures in Windows 0.24.25

Create a model from the same prompt box. The reference-facing surface can now display fine markings and materials from the locally generated image. A fitted camera view and a depth test limit the photo to visible facets. The remaining surface uses the reconstruction model’s predicted colors. The GLB includes its texture and opens offline.

A coarse pass locates the surface and a finer pass samples the geometry around it. Complex shapes use a smaller grid to fit the preview and export budget. The CPU side of the 3D worker can prepare while the image worker draws. The image worker must exit and deliver a verified reference before the 3D worker can use the GPU.

## Sculptor’s Bench, Windows 0.24.25

Rendered the old and new GLBs from the same red-panda reference with identical camera and light settings. The new model preserves the wood grain, tail stripes and facial markings. Rotating past the silhouette showed the predicted reverse surface. Corrected a material mismatch found during visual review. The mesh grew from 33,724 to 107,136 triangles and from 878,484 to 3,418,396 bytes. Both are interactive GLBs.

On an RTX 3060, clicking Create for the same ceramic-owl prompt and waiting for the saved preview took 34.8 seconds in 0.24.24 and 28.9 seconds in 0.24.25. These are individual runs with independent generated references. Separate fresh-process mesh-only timings with the identical red-panda image were 14.3, 15.9, 17.8 seconds on the prior build and 12.8, 16.4, 18.0 seconds on the new build. The latter two comparisons ran during compilation.

The packaged build generated a new 94,454-triangle owl with a self-contained photo texture. Verified its GLB digest across preview, export and replay, and rotated the saved model. Checked three window sizes, external-resource rejection, interrupted jobs, invalid mesh rejection and the shared worker’s two-message startup gate.
